holidays.name: National Gingerbread Cookie Day
holidays.description: Fire up the oven and let the spicy-sweet smell of ginger, cinnamon, and molasses take over your kitchen. Today is for baking, decorating, and nibbling gingerbread people, stars, and trees until nothing is left but crumbs and icing smudges.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It's celebrated every November 21 as the holiday baking season gets going.
holidays.funFact: Queen Elizabeth I of England is said to have served guests gingerbread likenesses of themselves at court. That makes her an early pioneer of edible portraits.

holidays.name: World Hello Day
holidays.description: Today the whole planet is encouraged to say hello to at least ten people. It's a small, silly, and surprisingly powerful way to spread friendliness. Wave at a neighbor, greet a stranger, or text an old friend a simple hi.
holidays.origin: World Hello Day began in 1973. It was a response to the Yom Kippur War, and people were encouraged to use simple greetings to promote peace. It has since spread to people in well over a hundred countries.
holidays.funFact: The idea is that personal communication is a better route to peace than conflict. Leaders are encouraged to settle disputes by talking.

holidays.name: National Stuffing Day
holidays.description: Just before Thanksgiving, this day puts the starring side dish in the spotlight. Cooks everywhere can argue happily about whether it's stuffing or dressing, and whether it goes inside the bird or in a casserole dish.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It's celebrated each November 21, which is conveniently close to Thanksgiving.
holidays.funFact: Stuffing is very old. Recipes for seasoned bread and herb fillings go back to ancient Roman cookbooks.
